the WMAP five-year catalog contains 390 sources with flux density greater than 2 Jy at 94 GHz, and that 99 of the WMAP 94 GHz sources have been found in the CMB-free V and W band maps, and are not strongly polarizied.
the WMAP five-year catalog is complete for sources with a flux density of 2 Jy and greater, and is 95% complete for sources with flux densities between 0.6 and 2 Jy.

the study of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropy, and the study of extragalactic point sources.
the detection of point sources in the WMAP maps, and with their characterization in terms of fluxes, polarization, variability, and spectra.
the study of the microwave background radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WMAP has not found any new sources of radio emission, but has confirmed the existence of the sources already found by other radio experiments.
WMAP has found 389 point sources with SNR greater or equal to 4.7 and 98 sources with SNR > 4.7, of which 97 are identified with radio sources.
the WMAP 1-year, 3-year and 5-year catalogs are complete for regions away from the galctic plane to a 1.6 Jy limit, and the 5-year catalog is complete for the whole sky to a 2.0 Jy limit.

the five-year source list is complete for sources away from the galaxian plane, and that the source list is dominated by radio galaxies, but that a small fraction are stars, AGN and other sources.

the sky is very complex at the WMAP resolution.
